questions_and_answers.question: Last night we went to bed late.

answers.answer: Anoche nos acostamos tarde.

questions_and_answers.question: This morning I got up at ten.

answers.answer: Esta mañana me levanté a las diez.

questions_and_answers.question: Yesterday I stayed at home.

answers.answer: Ayer me quedé en la casa.

questions_and_answers.question: They stayed in the city.

answers.answer: Ellos se quedaron en la ciudad.

questions_and_answers.question: We never complain about anything.

answers.answer: Nosotros nunca nos quejamos de nada.

questions_and_answers.question: We’re already used to hearing Spanish spoken.

answers.answer: Ya nos acostumbramos a oír hablar español.

questions_and_answers.question: She moved last week.

answers.answer: Ella se mudó de casa la semana pasada.

questions_and_answers.question: She didn’t say goodbye to us.

answers.answer: No se despidió de nosotros.

questions_and_answers.question: Afterward, we got in touch with her.

answers.answer: Después nos comunicamos con ella.

questions_and_answers.question: I was very happy.

answers.answer: Yo me alegré mucho.

questions_and_answers.question: I never complain.

answers.answer: Yo nunca me quejo.

questions_and_answers.question: We’re going to move to a pretty house.

answers.answer: Vamos a mudarnos a una casa bonita.

questions_and_answers.question: That boy’s going to fall and break his head.

answers.answer: Ese muchacho se va a caer y va a romperse la cabeza.

questions_and_answers.question: I’m getting nervous.

answers.answer: Me estoy poniendo nervioso.

questions_and_answers.question: Now I’m shaving late.

answers.answer: Ahora estoy afeitándome tarde.

questions_and_answers.question: We’re staying here every afternoon.

answers.answer: Nos estamos quedando aquí todas las tardes.

questions_and_answers.question: Why are you complaining about the furniture?

answers.answer: ¿Por qué se está quejando Ud. de los muebles?

questions_and_answers.question: They are going to change clothes.

answers.answer: Ellos van a cambiarse de ropa.

questions_and_answers.question: It’s getting late.

answers.answer: Se está haciendo tarde.

questions_and_answers.question: We’re going to bed.

answers.answer: Nos vamos a acostar.

questions_and_answers.question: When are you going to shave?

answers.answer: ¿Cuándo se va a afeitar Ud.?

questions_and_answers.question: Are you all going to get up late tomorrow?

answers.answer: ¿Van a levantarse tarde mañana?

questions_and_answers.question: Tonight I’m going to bed late.

answers.answer: Esta noche me voy a acostar tarde.

questions_and_answers.question: He’s going to bed late now.

answers.answer: Él se está acostando tarde ahora.

articles.text: This lesson explains Spanish reflexive clitic pronouns and their use in the present tense, as well as how to form the periphrastic future with reflexive verbs. A reflexive pronoun indicates that the subject performs the action on itself (e.g., *me levanto* – I get up). In Spanish, reflexive pronouns always agree with the subject. In periphrastic future constructions, reflexive pronouns may appear before the conjugated verb or attached to the infinitive or gerund.
